answers.evidence:
**Live server (uvicorn, two curls 1s apart)** — ran on port 8123 (8000/8080 were taken by a pre-existing service):

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8123/health          → {"status":"ok","uptime_seconds":0.0}
# sleep 1
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8123/health          → {"status":"ok","uptime_seconds":1.01135}
```

First call lazy-inits and reports ~0 (pre-fix it would report ~1,786,559,000 s = epoch); second call grows by ~1 s. Server log: `Started server process`, `Application startup complete`.

**Regression suite** — `pytest test_harness.py -v`: **6 passed**:

| Test | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `test_health_uptime_is_small_when_super_init_skipped` | `BrokenSubclass` (no `super().__init__()`) → uptime < 60 s, not epoch |
| `test_health_uptime_is_small_without_any_init` | Plain default-constructed `BaseHarness` lazy-inits too |
| `test_uptime_grows_monotonically_over_time` | `sleep(1.1)` → uptime delta ≥ 1.0 s |
| `test_lazy_init_happens_only_once` | Repeated `health()` calls never reset the clock |
| `test_positive_started_at_is_respected` | A user-preset `_started_at` (e.g. 42 s ago) is honored, not overridden |
| `test_epoch_never_reported` | 50 fresh broken instances all report < 60 s |

Edge cases considered: class-default `0.0` vs. user-set positive start (both correct); repeated calls stay monotonic; the lazy write via `self` keeps the class attribute clean for future instances. Verified on Python 3.14.4, FastAPI 0.141.1, uvicorn 0.52.1.
